claim: Expert parallelism requires a token all-to-all every layer, and on a system without NVLink and without P2P atomics that all-to-all goes through the host bridge and 'tanks performance', whereas TP needs only per-layer all-reduce which NCCL ring handles tolerably over PCIe.
stance_target: cc-3's exclusion of EP from the viable topology set on a no-P2P fabric
scope_conditions: Community wiki for no-NVLink workstation Blackwell GPUs; inference/serving scope; no measured numbers
quoted_support: Expert parallelism ... demands a token all-to-all every layer. On a system without NVLink and without P2P atomics, that all-to-all goes through the host bridge and tanks performance. Tensor parallelism only requires per-layer all-reduce. NCCL ring all-reduce works tolerably over PCIe and the host bridge

claim: The wiki's bandwidth arithmetic puts EP at ~1 MB per layer of cross-GPU traffic versus TP at ~12 KB per layer at H=8192, N=4, top-k=8 — a ~80x difference — and claims rewriting EP as TP 'often eliminates 80%+ of communication overhead'.
stance_target: The claim that EP is the wrong topology on this fabric and TP is the cheaper alternative
scope_conditions: H=8192, N=4, top-k=8, per token per layer; inference decode (B=1, T=1) for the TP figure
quoted_support: EP: ~16 x 8 x 8192 = ~1 MB per layer of cross-GPU traffic / TP: ~12 KB per layer of cross-GPU traffic / A ~80x difference.

claim: The wiki's scope is inference engines (vLLM, sglang, TRT-LLM) and it supplies no training measurement, so it cannot satisfy cc-3(c)'s requirement for a host-staged EP or TP TRAINING run at >=1B params.
stance_target: Whether this source can reopen EP/TP for training
scope_conditions: Wiki page 'EP-to-TP rewriting'; config examples are serving-engine YAML
quoted_support: In an inference-engine config: # Before (EP) tensor_parallel_size: 1 expert_parallel_size: 4
